correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, exact reciprocal scaling gives integer lengths a=n(n+1)/(2g), b=n(n+3)/(2g), c=(n+2)(n+3)/(2g), g=gcd(n,3). Reversing translates by (b+c,c-a,-a-b). This is the first return to [0,L) of rotation by t=b+c on circle S=a+2b+c, with the middle branch taking two rotations. Since gcd(s=a+b,t=b+c)=1, every fractional-offset orbit visits the L unit cells of the section exactly once and T has least period L=3(n+1)(n+2)/(2g) for EVERY real point, including half-open boundaries. Independent exact integer-cell traversal for n=1..60 gave a single L-cycle each. On R_{11,7}, exact D=27720 scales four lengths to (252,308,385,495), shifts (1188,628,-65,-945) and exhaustive 1440-cell cycles (694,373,373), giving period masses 694/27720 and 746/27720. This finite contrast is exhaustive; the infinite n proof is not extrapolated from testing.

originality.rationale: Hooper–Rafi–Randecker define R_{m,n} in their Remark 7, show finite rational branch periodicity in Proposition 4, and explicitly leave pair classification open. Their printed examples have multiple periods but do not state the n+3,n arithmetic formula. Linero Bas–Soler López (2025) classify possible oriented 3-IET period SETS and give Rauzy first-return machinery; generic 3-IET rotation theory could reproduce the mechanism but no checked statement supplies this exact reciprocal modulus-three least-period and four-piece masses. Best-of-knowledge original arithmetic solution, not a new induced-rotation theorem.
